tldr.after: An oncogene is an activated form of a growth-promoting gene. Its presence alone does not prove that the cancer depends on it or that a particular drug will help.

summary.after: Normal proto-oncogenes participate in cell growth and survival. Particular sequence changes, extra copies or rearrangements can increase or redirect their activity. Whether an alteration drives disease, creates a dependency or supplies a useful treatment target depends on its functional and disease context.

summary.after: Tumour-suppressor genes contribute to growth restraint, genome maintenance and responses to damage. Some cancers disable both useful copies; in other settings reduced dosage or interference by an altered protein matters. The exact variant, copy state and functional context determine what has been lost.

tldr.after: Angiogenesis is the growth of new blood vessels from existing vessels. Vessel number, blood flow, transport and oxygen delivery are different measurements.

summary.after: Endothelial cells form new vessels in response to signals such as VEGF and its receptors, during normal development and repair as well as disease. Cancer populations can obtain vascular access through new growth or use of existing vessels. Altering this system can affect delivery and local conditions, but a vessel or expression measurement alone does not establish treatment benefit.

after: Angiogenesis creates new vessels from existing vessels through endothelial-cell growth and signalling, including VEGF and its receptors. It also occurs in development and repair. A tumour can obtain blood by other routes: Holash and colleagues observed co-option of existing vessels in their tumour models. Vessel structure, perfusion, permeability, tracer transport and oxygenation are separate measurements. Density counts structures within an area; perfusion concerns blood flow through a region; permeability concerns material crossing vessel walls; a tracer readout follows a particular probe. Oxygen availability also depends on diffusion and cellular consumption.

Blocking vascular signalling can change vessel integrity and transport as well as vessel number. Tong studied transport after VEGFR2 blockade; Winkler studied a temporary oxygenation and radiation-response window in mouse brain-tumour models. These are conditional experimental findings. They do not establish a universal dose, treatment schedule or clinical benefit, and excessive loss of useful vessels can limit delivery.

In E2100, 722 participants with metastatic breast cancer were randomised to paclitaxel with or without bevacizumab. Median progression-free survival was 11.8 versus 5.9 months; median overall survival was 26.7 versus 25.2 months, with P=0.16 for overall survival. The progression-free result did not establish an overall-survival benefit. The FDA withdrawn-approvals table records withdrawal of the US first-line HER2-negative metastatic-breast indication on 18 November 2011. That decision concerns a named indication and jurisdiction.

For a vascular measurement, retain the site, region, date, treatment exposure, measured area and counting or imaging method. Vessels per square millimetre describes density; contrast exchange describes a particular transport measurement; VEGF RNA describes expression. None is a direct substitute for oxygen measurement. A vessel-growth mechanism or VEGF signal alone does not establish dependence, selective tumour starvation, safety or individual treatment benefit.

Fictional equal-area fields contain four versus two vessel structures, while separately measured tracer values are 100 versus 160 arbitrary units. The second field has fewer vessels and a higher tracer readout. This is logically possible without establishing its oxygen level or treatment benefit. Drawn arrows are not measured flow rates. A roads analogy or workflow from vessels to delivery organises the questions; each functional step still needs evidence.

tldr.after: Metastasis is the establishment of cancer at a distant site. Finding cells in transit or in another tissue does not by itself demonstrate sustained distant growth.

summary.after: Cancer cells may leave a primary site, travel through blood or lymph, reach another tissue and establish a growing lesion. Many steps can fail. Regional lymph-node involvement differs from distant metastasis, and the distant deposit retains the identity of the primary cancer. Clinical interpretation depends on the represented sites and disease context.

summary.after: Cancer cells interact with neighbouring immune and stromal cells, vessels, extracellular material and physical conditions. summary.after: Related cancer-cell populations can differ in inherited features and in their representation over time or across sites. tldr.after: The hallmarks organise research on cancer capabilities. The framework has changed over time and is not a diagnostic checklist or a treatment-selection test.

summary.after: The hallmarks framework groups recurring capabilities and enabling processes involved in cancer. Its 2000, 2011 and 2022 versions distinguish core capabilities from emerging or provisional additions. Different cells and their surroundings can contribute, and a measurement of one process does not establish all the others.

after: The hallmarks are a versioned research framework, not a diagnostic checklist, stage, clinical assay standard or a demand that every cell independently perform every capability. The 2000 proposal contained six capabilities. The 2011 account retained six, added two emerging capabilities and described two enabling characteristics. In the 2022 account, the two emerging capabilities joined the eight core capabilities.

The eight core capabilities are sustained growth signalling, evasion of growth restraints, resistance to cell death, sustained replicative capacity, obtaining a blood supply, invasion and distant colonisation, altered metabolism, and evasion of immune control. These are distinct processes: division speed does not measure replicative capacity, and a growth-related gene alteration does not establish invasion or immune escape. Vascular access can include existing vessels, not only new vessel growth.

Genome instability and mutation, and tumour-promoting inflammation, are enabling characteristics in the stated framework; not every mutation matters and not all inflammation promotes cancer. Hanahan’s 2022 additions remain at different explanatory levels: plasticity as a proposed capability, nonmutational epigenetic reprogramming and microbiomes as possible enablers, and senescent cells as microenvironment participants. They are not four equivalent established core hallmarks.

Capabilities can depend on cooperation with surrounding cells. To measure one, specify the process: division, death, invasion, vascular relations, metabolism or immune function. An RNA program is not a direct measurement of every capability or metabolic flux, and there is no universal hallmark unit or cutoff selecting treatment. In a fictional mutation-rich report, an enabling characteristic alone neither establishes distant disease nor proves those mutations caused the behaviour. A framework diagram organises concepts and provisional additions; it does not measure them in a specimen.

Fibroblasts are cells; stroma is a broader compartment that also includes extracellular matrix, vascular structures and other cells. Fibroblasts can produce and remodel matrix and exchange signals with neighbouring cells. In the solid-tumour settings discussed here, a stromal signal is not automatically a malignant-epithelial signal. Sahai and colleagues describe diverse origins and states, without one marker or one effect shared by every cancer-associated fibroblast.

Ohlund and colleagues described alpha-smooth-muscle-actin-high myofibroblastic fibroblasts near pancreatic cancer cells and IL-6-producing inflammatory populations farther away in pancreatic models and samples. This is not an exhaustive classification of breast stroma or a permanent job assignment for each cell. Ozdemir reported that depletion of selected alpha-smooth-muscle-actin-positive myofibroblasts worsened disease and immunosuppression in pancreatic mouse models. Removing all fibroblasts is not a general treatment conclusion. The indexed 2015 correction is linked; its body was unavailable for this review, so no correction-specific figure claim is adopted.

Immune exclusion describes immune-cell positions relative to malignant nests. Salmon studied how matrix architecture affected T-cell movement in viable human lung-tumour slices, including a collagenase perturbation. That experiment does not show that a fibroblast-rich breast specimen is immune-excluded or that removing its stroma would help. The locations and the proposed mechanism need separate evidence.

A fibroblast assessment may use fixed sections or appropriately prepared cells; sectioning and dissociation consume finite material. Report the defined marker-positive populations, cells per area or another stated denominator, cell states and positions relative to tumour structures. Retain marker combinations, morphology, cell assignment, specificity and sampled regions. There is no universal CAF-high threshold establishing function or treatment benefit. Bulk RNA can increase because there are more cells or because each cell expresses more; dissociation also loses the spatial map.

In a fictional breast section with many fibroblasts and collagen but no scored immune-cell positions, immune exclusion has not been measured. First map the immune cells against tumour nests, then test candidate causes. A neighbourhood drawing can locate fibroblasts, matrix and vessels and suggest possible signals or remodelling. It does not measure movement or show that every fibroblast promotes cancer.

after: Hypoxia is reduced local oxygen availability relative to tissue needs. It is different from complete absence of oxygen and from a permanent defect in mitochondria. Delivery, functioning vessels, diffusion distance and oxygen consumption all matter, and conditions change across regions and time. Removing tissue interrupts delivery, so collection and handling can change the state being studied.

HIF-1 contains alpha and beta protein subunits. Under oxygen-replete conditions, oxygen-dependent modification of the alpha subunit enables VHL-associated degradation; limiting that regulation can stabilise it. Jaakkola and the Semenza review describe this mechanism and additional regulation. HIF RNA, alpha-protein stability and the resulting transcriptional response are different quantities. Alternative molecular regulation can alter HIF, so neither protein staining nor an RNA signature is a calibrated oxygen meter.

The cited 2019 spatial method used mouse pancreatic-cancer xenografts, a perfusion tracer and separate hypoxia and proliferation markers, with cell segmentation and distance analysis. Its model, preparation and marker definitions matter. It does not supply a universal human vessel-distance cutoff or establish that changing oxygen will reverse immune exclusion or improve treatment. Producing lactate while oxygen is available, often called the Warburg effect, also does not by itself establish hypoxia or a survival dependency.

An oxygen study may measure local partial pressure in situ or use suitable tissue for a defined response-protein or RNA assay. Report which output was measured. Retain region, time, calibration, handling, cell identity and factors that can alter HIF independently of oxygen; destructive assays use finite material. Thresholds must fit the method and purpose. Vessel density is not flow, HIF abundance is not oxygen concentration, and a specimen average can hide poorly oxygenated regions.

In a fictional biopsy with a high hypoxia-response score, the score alone gives neither an exact oxygen level nor proof that every region is hypoxic. tldr.after: An evolutionary framework explains how inherited variation, selection and chance change cancer populations. Sampling and model assumptions limit what can be inferred for one tumour.

summary.after:
The claim. Cancer proceeds by Darwinian evolution within the body: heritable variation (mutations, epigenetic states, chromosome changes) arises in a founding clone, natural selection in the tissue favours variants that grow or survive better, and the tumour diversifies into subclones. The ecological extension (Merlo, Maley, Gatenby) adds that cells compete for space, oxygen and nutrients, cooperate through shared growth factors and face predators in the immune system, so a tumour is an ecosystem and therapy is a perturbation of it.

Who and when. Nowell's 1976 Science paper The clonal evolution of tumor cell populations stated the theory and predicted that each patient's tumour would be genetically unique and that therapy would select resistant variants. Cairns (1975) argued that tissue architecture limits somatic evolution. Merlo, Pepper, Reid and Maley (2006) set out cancer as an evolutionary and ecological process; Greaves and Maley reviewed the evidence in 2012; Gerlinger and Swanton's 2012 multi-region sequencing of kidney cancer showed branched evolution directly; Gatenby proposed adaptive therapy in 2009 and Zhang and colleagues reported a pilot in prostate cancer in 2017; Sottoriva and Graham proposed the Big Bang model of colorectal tumour growth in 2015.

Evidence for. Multi-region and single-cell studies can reconstruct sampled populations as related clones with a truncal set of early mutations and branches that differ between regions and metastases. Resistance arises by selection of pre-existing or newly mutated clones (EGFR T790M and C797S in lung cancer, KRAS clones under EGFR antibodies in colorectal cancer, BCR::ABL1 T315I in chronic myeloid leukaemia), and repeated circulating tumour DNA measurements can track detected variants subject to sampling and assay limits. Outcome associations depend on the cancer, measure and setting. Mel Greaves' studies of childhood leukaemia in twins showed the founding clone can form in the womb years before diagnosis.

Evidence against and limits. Neutral and early-burst models offer alternatives to continuous subclonal selection, but a frequency-model fit alone does not prove neutral evolution, and some change by punctuated catastrophe (chromothripsis, whole-genome doubling) rather than gradual accumulation. Evolution is hard to predict for an individual patient, and the theory does not by itself say what starts the process. Randomised evidence that evolution-informed dosing beats standard dosing is still awaited.

Predictions that held or failed. Held in particular settings: resistant populations can emerge under targeted treatment, and combinations or monitoring can inform further treatment; rechallenge with an EGFR antibody works after resistant clones recede (CHRONOS). Failed: the Goldie-Coldman prediction that alternating non-cross-resistant regimens would improve outcomes was not borne out in trials; efforts to model a tumour's trajectory precisely enough to time therapy remain experimental.

Therapies that came from it. Combination therapy as a principle, minimal residual disease monitoring, liquid biopsy surveillance for resistance mutations, adaptive and intermittent dosing (adaptive therapy in prostate cancer), evolutionary herding and collateral sensitivity, and the mathematical oncology programme that models these dynamics. It is the theory the driver and passenger model feeds into, the ageing tissue view builds on (aged tissue changes what is selected), and the immunoediting theory applies to the immune system as predator.

Status: evolutionary change is supported by multiple research designs. Inference about an individual tumour and benefit from a particular evolution-informed treatment strategy require their own sampling, model and comparative evidence.

tldr.after: Cancer cells interact with surrounding tissue and immune cells. Inflammation and stromal responses can help or restrain cancer, with effects depending on the population and context.

summary.after:
The claim. Cancer cells interact with fibroblasts, macrophages, endothelium and other neighbours through signals and structural changes. Some processes resemble wound repair. Chronic inflammatory conditions can contribute to particular cancers, while immune and stromal responses can also restrain disease. In the strong form, the microenvironment is where cancer begins; in the mainstream form, it is an enabling characteristic and a full participant.

Who and when. Virchow described leukocytes in tumours in 1863 and proposed that irritation causes cancer. Dvorak's 1986 essay noted that tumour stroma is generated by the same vascular leak, fibrin deposition and fibroblast activation as granulation tissue. Balkwill and Mantovani (2001) and Coussens and Werb (2002) set out the molecular case for inflammation as a cause; Hanahan and Coussens (2012) catalogued the recruited cells as 'accessories to the crime'; Schäfer and Werner (2008) revisited the overhealing wound. Judah Folkman's angiogenesis hypothesis (1971) and Mina Bissell's microenvironment work are part of the same lineage.

Evidence for. Infections and inflammatory conditions cause cancer: Helicobacter pylori and gastric cancer, hepatitis B and C and liver cancer, ulcerative colitis and colorectal cancer, asbestos and mesothelioma, reflux and oesophageal adenocarcinoma. Long-term aspirin reduces colorectal cancer incidence and cancer death in randomised trial follow-up (Rothwell 2011). Tumour stroma has the cell types and signals of a healing wound, and particular fibroblast and macrophage populations can promote growth, invasion or immune exclusion, while others have different or opposing effects. Anti-inflammatory interleukin-1 beta blockade with canakinumab reduced incident lung cancer in the CANTOS cardiovascular trial. Inflammation became an enabling characteristic in the 2011 hallmarks.

Evidence against and limits. Many cancers arise without recognisable inflammation, and inflammation is also how the immune system attacks tumours: an inflammatory or T-cell-rich pattern alone does not establish benefit from a checkpoint inhibitor. Anti-inflammatory treatment of established cancer has largely failed: canakinumab did not improve survival in the CANOPY lung cancer trials, and matrix metalloproteinase inhibitors failed in the 1990s. The claim that the microenvironment initiates cancer is hard to separate from the mutations that inflammation causes.

Predictions that held or failed. Held in defined prevention settings: treating an infection or preventing infection can reduce related cancer risk. Aspirin findings and stromal prognostic associations require their own populations, outcomes and safety context. Failed: anti-angiogenic therapy as a broad cure; its clinical effects vary by regimen and setting; anti-inflammatory drugs as treatment for established cancer; stroma depletion in pancreatic cancer (hyaluronidase failed in phase 3).

Therapies that came from it. Aspirin and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory chemoprevention, the HPV and hepatitis B vaccines and H. pylori eradication, anti-VEGF antibodies and kinase inhibitors, and the current trials of fibroblast, macrophage and interleukin targeting. The theory feeds the seed and soil hypothesis (the soil is a microenvironment), the immune surveillance theory and the hallmarks, and it carries forward the tissue organisation field theory's evidence in a form the mainstream accepts.

Status: established for inflammation's role in causing and promoting cancer and for the stroma as a participant; contested as the primary origin of cancer in place of mutation.

tldr.after: Immune responses can control cancer and select which populations persist. Immunoediting is a testable framework, not a way to assign a phase or recurrence risk from one scan.

summary.after:
The claim. Immune surveillance concerns recognition and control of transformed cells. Immunoediting adds selection of the populations that persist. Elimination, equilibrium and escape are conceptual processes that can coexist or occur independently. Their assignment requires evidence of control, restraint or outgrowth and its mechanism; they are not a compulsory calendar for every clinical cancer. The immune system therefore both protects against cancer and shapes the cancers that emerge.

Who and when. Ehrlich 1909; Burnet 1957 and 1970 and Thomas 1959 stated the surveillance hypothesis. Stutman's 1974 finding that athymic nude mice were no more prone to chemically induced tumours seemed to refute it. Shankaran, Old and Schreiber showed in 2001 that mice lacking lymphocytes or interferon-gamma signalling develop more tumours and that tumours from immunodeficient mice are more immunogenic, which is the signature of editing. Dunn and colleagues named immunoediting in 2002; Schreiber, Old and Smyth reviewed it in 2011. Allison's 1996 CTLA-4 blockade and Honjo's PD-1 discovery gave it its therapy; Chen and Mellman's cancer-immunity cycle (2013) is its clinical map.

Evidence for. Immunodeficient mice develop more spontaneous and induced tumours. Organ transplant recipients on immunosuppression have higher rates of many cancers, not only virus-driven ones. Immune-cell and outcome associations vary across cancers and measurements. Some tumour studies show neoantigen depletion or HLA loss consistent with editing, with other explanations and sampling limits still relevant. Checkpoint inhibitors produce durable remissions in melanoma, lung, kidney, bladder and mismatch repair-deficient cancers, while mutation count, candidate neoantigens or viral origin alone do not establish an individual response.

Evidence against and limits. Nude mice retain immune functions and are not a clean comparison of every immune mechanism; Shankaran also noted that they do not completely lack functional T cells. The episode illustrates the importance of the precise model. Most cancers arise in people with normal immunity, and the immune system also promotes cancer through inflammation. Equilibrium is difficult to observe directly in humans. Immunotherapy fails in most patients with pancreatic, prostate and brain cancers, and the reasons are only partly understood.

Predictions that held or failed. Held: releasing checkpoints unleashes anti-tumour immunity; particular studies find loss of recognised antigens under immune pressure; adoptive transfer of tumour-reactive T cells can cure. Failed: most therapeutic cancer vaccines of the 1990s and 2000s; the expectation that boosting immunity non-specifically (interferon, interleukin-2 in most settings) would be broadly effective.

Therapies that came from it. Checkpoint inhibitors (ipilimumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab and successors), CAR-T cells, tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy (lifileucel), T-cell engagers, neoantigen mRNA vaccines and the use of mutational burden and mismatch repair deficiency as predictive biomarkers. It applies clonal evolution to the immune system as predator, draws on the microenvironment view for the mechanisms of escape, and entered the hallmarks in 2011.

Status: model experiments and human observations support immune control and selection. They do not establish a universal sequence of phases, the fraction of all cancers prevented, or a personal recurrence forecast.

Koebel used immune perturbation in chemical-carcinogenesis mouse models to demonstrate equilibrium; a quiet scan alone is not such an experiment. Matsushita combined sequencing, antigen recognition and immune comparisons in mouse sarcoma to support selection of pre-existing antigen-distinct clones. Luksza followed 70 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas from 15 people longitudinally over ten years, comparing primary and recurrent tumours and modelling neoantigen quality and clonal fitness. Long-term survivors had stronger primary T-cell activity and recurrent tumours with fewer high-quality neoantigens under the model. This is human cohort and modelling evidence, not a vaccine experiment or direct observation of every selection event. Treatment and sampling history and model assumptions remain relevant.

In a fictional immune-pressure comparison, both arms begin with A/B counts of 80/20. Later, the control has 160/40 and the pressure arm 10/40. B is 20% versus 80% of the later populations, although its later count is 40 in both. Recognition and comparable conditions are separate evidence; a larger share does not mean that pressure created more B cells. summary.after: Some cancer cells rely strongly on an activated growth or survival driver. This differs from a conditional vulnerability caused by another loss and from dependence on a normal stress-support function. Controlled perturbations, appropriate comparators and clinical evidence answer different parts of the treatment question.

A mutation, stain or high RNA level does not by itself establish any of them or a therapeutic window relative to normal cells.

Weinstein introduced the addiction concept; Luo’s framework describes normal stress-support functions and discusses the proteasome in myeloma. The evidence type matters: a conceptual framework is not a clinical selection assay. This historical dose-group observation is neither prescribing advice nor a comparative-survival estimate.

BCR-ABL/imatinib and HER2/trastuzumab are named driver-dependence examples. Farmer and Bryant demonstrated sensitivity of BRCA-deficient laboratory models to PARP inhibition. A synthetic-lethal design compares the relevant single losses with the paired loss. A backup-pathway analogy is useful but does not make every interaction simple redundancy. Most drug combinations are not established synthetic-lethal pairs; a tumour’s existing loss plus one intervention differs from inducing two losses experimentally. PARP and ATR inhibition should not be called a universal synthetic-lethal pair; each experiment must establish the interaction in its specified context. The authors called this induced synthetic lethality. It is model evidence, with no patient-benefit claim.

In a fictional repair-loss experiment, cells lacking one function die after a second perturbation, while matched restored cells survive. The restoration comparison supports conditionality rather than general toxicity, with exposure and off-target controls still needed. The same tumour may have driver, conditional and normal-support dependencies. A decision diagram classifies the function removed; it does not demonstrate that the dependency exists or establish treatment benefit.

Extracellular matrix includes fibrous proteins such as collagen and fibronectin and carbohydrate-rich molecules such as proteoglycans. Cells produce it; the matrix is not itself a living-cell population. Basement membrane is a specialised matrix, while connective tissue and stroma include cells as well. Production, enzymatic breakdown and crosslinking can change its amount and organisation over time.

Levental and Paszek studied how crosslinking, matrix rigidity, integrin-linked signals and cell tension affected mammary-cell organisation and invasion in experimental systems. These findings do not make every collagen-rich tissue stiff, invasive or drug resistant. Integrins connect matrix conditions to chemical and mechanical cell responses; a matrix can offer routes or restrictions, rather than forming one universal solid wall.

Amount, fibre orientation, pore architecture, density, stiffness and cell behaviour are different features. Stiffness describes resistance to deformation, often expressed as a modulus in pascals; the result depends on the measurement scale, preparation and loading. Collagen-stained area and collagen RNA do not directly measure stiffness. Salmon’s viable human lung-tumour slices linked architecture and T-cell movement under the studied conditions; the result does not establish the mechanism in every breast tumour.

Fixed sections can support stains or imaging, while mechanics and live migration need suitable preparations for those questions. Sectioning and destructive experiments use finite material. Report stained area, orientation, local architecture or the specified mechanical output, retaining region selection, preparation, image method, loading and cell identity. There is no universal ECM-high threshold establishing immune exclusion or treatment benefit. An RNA profile does not reconstruct matrix architecture, and a stain does not measure migration or whole-tumour mechanics.

In a fictional pair of equal-area fields with eight equal-size fibres each, equal drawn collagen area can accompany different architecture. Independently stipulated mean T-cell speeds of 4 micrometres per minute do not establish equal directions, entry into tumour nests, contact with cancer cells or stiffness. Cell positions outside nests alone do not show that matrix caused them; other signals may contribute. Separate the structural observation, live movement measurement and causal perturbation, then assess any clinical claim with its own evidence.

Candidate epitope selection considers presentation and immune recognition; these require evidence beyond mutation count or predicted binding. HLA genotype shapes which peptides can be displayed. Escape variants explain acquired resistance to checkpoint blockade and CAR-T (CD19 loss).
